questions.text: 1 मोल MnO4⁻ को MnO2 में अपचयित करने के लिए आवश्यक आवेश है
questions.text_english: The charge required for the reduction of 1 mol of MnO4⁻ to MnO2 is
questions.solution: In MnO4⁻, the oxidation state of Mn is +7. In MnO2, the oxidation state of Mn is +4. The change in oxidation state = +7 to +4 = a gain of 3 electrons per Mn atom. Therefore, for 1 mole of MnO4⁻, 3 moles of electrons (3 Faradays) are required. Option A (1 F) is too low; option C (5 F) corresponds to reduction to Mn²⁺ in acidic medium; option D (6 F) corresponds to reduction to Mn⁰. Hence, the correct answer is 3 F.
questions.solution_hindi: MnO4⁻ में Mn की ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था +7 है और MnO2 में +4 है। अतः ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था में परिवर्तन = 3 (3 इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रति Mn परमाणु)। इसलिए 1 मोल MnO4⁻ के लिए 3 F आवेश की आवश्यकता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन गलत है?
questions.text_english: Which among the following is a false statement?

options.A: शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया वेग अभिकारक की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता से स्वतंत्र होता है।
options.B: शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया की अर्द्ध-आयु, वेग स्थिरांक के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।
options.C: किसी अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता शून्य हो सकती है।
options.D: प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए t1/2 = 0.693/k

options_english.A: Rate of zero order reaction is independent of initial concentration of reactant.
options_english.B: Half-life of a zero order reaction is inversely proportional to the rate constant.
options_english.C: Molecularity of a reaction may be zero.
options_english.D: For a first order reaction, t1/2 = 0.693/k.

questions.solution: Molecularity is defined as the number of molecules (atoms, ions, or radicals) that collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction step. It is always a positive integer (1, 2, or rarely 3) and can never be zero or a fraction. Therefore, statement C is false. Statements A and D are standard correct facts about zero and first order reactions respectively. For a zero order reaction, t1/2 = [A]0 / 2k, which is indeed proportional to the initial concentration and inversely proportional to k — making statement B correct.
questions.solution_hindi: आण्विकता किसी प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया में भाग लेने वाले अणुओं की संख्या है, यह हमेशा धनात्मक पूर्णांक (1, 2 या 3) होती है। इसलिए आण्विकता शून्य नहीं हो सकती — विकल्प C गलत कथन है।

questions.text: अणुओं की संख्या जो किसी प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया में परस्पर अभिक्रिया करते हैं, एक माप होती है
questions.text_english: The number of molecules that react with each other in an elementary reaction is a measure of the:
questions.solution: By definition, molecularity of a reaction is the number of reacting species (molecules, atoms, or ions) that come together and collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction step. Activation energy relates to the energy barrier, stoichiometry refers to molar ratios in a balanced equation, and order is determined experimentally from the rate law. Hence option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: आण्विकता की परिभाषा के अनुसार, प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया में एक साथ टकराने वाले अणुओं की संख्या आण्विकता कहलाती है। अतः सही उत्तर C है।

questions.text: [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास वाला तत्व है
questions.text_english: The element having [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ electronic configuration is
questions.solution: Copper (Cu, Z=29) has the anomalous electronic configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ due to the extra stability of a completely filled d-orbital. The expected configuration would be [Ar]3d⁹4s², but one electron from 4s shifts to 3d to achieve the more stable fully-filled 3d subshell. Zinc (Zn) has [Ar]3d¹⁰4s², Chromium (Cr) has [Ar]3d⁵4s¹, and Manganese (Mn) has [Ar]3d⁵4s². Hence, option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: कॉपर (Cu, Z=29) का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ है क्योंकि पूर्ण भरे 3d उपकोश की विशेष स्थायित्व के कारण 4s से एक इलेक्ट्रॉन 3d में स्थानांतरित हो जाता है।

questions.text: संकुल आयन [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]²⁺ तथा [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]²⁺ कहलाते हैं
questions.text_english: The complex ions [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]²⁺ and [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]²⁺ are called
questions.solution: Linkage isomers arise when an ambidentate ligand (a ligand capable of coordinating through two different atoms) bonds to the metal through different donor atoms. In [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]²⁺, the nitrite ligand coordinates through nitrogen (N-bonded, nitro form), while in [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]²⁺, it coordinates through oxygen (O-bonded, nitrito form). Since the same ligand (NO2⁻) bonds through different atoms, these are linkage isomers. Hence option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: बंधनी समावयवता (Linkage isomerism) तब होती है जब द्विदंती लिगेंड विभिन्न दाता परमाणुओं के माध्यम से धातु से जुड़ता है। NO2⁻ N-द्वारा या O-द्वारा जुड़ सकता है, अतः ये बंधनी समावयवी हैं।

questions.text: प्रतिचुंबकीय स्पीशीज़ है [परमाणु संख्या : Co = 27, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
questions.text_english: The diamagnetic species is: [At. No. Co = 27, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
questions.solution: In [Ni(CN)4]²⁻, Ni is in +2 oxidation state (d⁸ configuration). CN⁻ is a strong field ligand that causes pairing of electrons, resulting in a square planar geometry with dsp² hybridization and no unpaired electrons — hence diamagnetic. In [NiCl4]²⁻, Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand giving tetrahedral geometry with 2 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic). [Fe(CN)6]³⁻ has Fe³⁺ (d⁵) with 1 unpaired electron; [CoF6]³⁻ has Co³⁺ (d⁶) with 4 unpaired electrons due to weak field F⁻. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: [Ni(CN)4]²⁻ में Ni²⁺ (d⁸) है और CN⁻ प्रबल क्षेत्र लिगेंड होने के कारण dsp² संकरण और वर्गाकार समतलीय संरचना बनाता है जिसमें कोई अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉन नहीं होता। अतः यह प्रतिचुंबकीय है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के लिए कौन सा सही IUPAC नाम है? (बेंजीन वलय पर para स्थिति में CH3 और Cl प्रतिस्थापी)
questions.text_english: Which is the correct IUPAC name for the compound with CH3 at the top and Cl at the bottom in para position on a benzene ring?
questions.solution: In IUPAC nomenclature for disubstituted benzenes, we choose the substituent that comes first alphabetically to decide numbering — here Cl (chloro) comes before methyl alphabetically, so the carbon bearing Cl gets the lower locant (1), and the CH3 group is at position 4. Therefore the correct name is 1-Chloro-4-Methylbenzene (option C). Option D (1-Methyl-4-Chlorobenzene) gives higher locant to methyl, violating the alphabetical priority rule for numbering. Options A and B are incorrect common names.
questions.solution_hindi: IUPAC नामकरण में वर्णमाला क्रम के अनुसार Cl (क्लोरो) को CH3 (मेथिल) से पहले प्राथमिकता मिलती है, इसलिए Cl वाले कार्बन को स्थान 1 तथा CH3 को स्थान 4 मिलता है। सही नाम 1-क्लोरो-4-मेथिलबेंज़ीन है।

questions.text: द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉल की क्रोमिक ऐनहाइड्राइड (CrO3) के साथ ऑक्सीकरण अभिक्रिया के बाद क्या बनेगा?
questions.text_english: What will be formed after oxidation reaction of secondary alcohol with chromic anhydride (CrO3)?
questions.solution: When a secondary alcohol (R-CHOH-R') is oxidized with CrO3 (chromic anhydride), the product is a ketone (R-CO-R'). This is because the secondary alcohol has the OH group on a carbon bonded to two alkyl groups; oxidation removes two hydrogen atoms (one from OH and one from the CH) to give a C=O group flanked by two carbon chains, which is a ketone. Primary alcohols give aldehydes (which can be further oxidized to carboxylic acids), not secondary alcohols. Hence option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉल (R-CHOH-R') को CrO3 से ऑक्सीकृत करने पर कीटोन (R-CO-R') बनता है क्योंकि -OH समूह दो कार्बन श्रृंखलाओं के बीच होता है।

questions.text: फीनॉल का सैलिसिलिक अम्ल में रूपांतरण निम्न में से किसके द्वारा किया जा सकता है?
questions.text_english: The conversion of phenol to salicylic acid can be accomplished by
questions.solution: The Kolbe reaction (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction) converts phenol to salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). In this reaction, sodium phenoxide is treated with CO2 under pressure at about 125°C, followed by acidification, to introduce a -COOH group ortho to the -OH group on the ring. The Reimer-Tiemann reaction introduces a -CHO group (giving salicylaldehyde, not salicylic acid). Friedel-Crafts and coupling reactions serve entirely different purposes. Hence option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: कोल्बे अभिक्रिया (Kolbe-Schmitt) में सोडियम फीनॉक्साइड को CO2 के साथ दाब पर गर्म किया जाता है जिससे सैलिसिलिक अम्ल बनता है। अतः सही उत्तर C है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा/से प्रोटीन के विकृतीकरण का उदाहरण है/हैं?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is/are examples of denaturation of protein?
questions.solution: Denaturation of proteins involves the disruption of secondary and tertiary structure without breaking peptide bonds, leading to loss of biological activity. Coagulation of egg white (albumin) on heating and curdling of milk (casein) on adding acid are both classic examples of denaturation where the protein loses its native structure and precipitates. Clotting of blood is an enzymatic cascade process, not a denaturation example. Therefore, both A and B are correct, making option D the right answer.
questions.solution_hindi: विकृतीकरण (Denaturation) में प्रोटीन की द्वितीयक और तृतीयक संरचना नष्ट होती है। अंडे का जमना और दही का जमना दोनों विकृतीकरण के उदाहरण हैं। अतः सही उत्तर D है।

questions.text: न्यूक्लियोटाइड आपस में किस बंध द्वारा जुड़े होते हैं?
questions.text_english: Nucleotides are joined together by
questions.solution: In nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), nucleotides are covalently joined to each other through phosphodiester linkages. The phosphate group forms ester bonds with the 3'-OH of one nucleotide's sugar and the 5'-OH of the next nucleotide's sugar, creating the sugar-phosphate backbone of the strand. Glycosidic linkages connect the nitrogenous base to the sugar within a nucleotide. Peptide bonds join amino acids in proteins. Hydrogen bonds form between complementary base pairs on opposite strands but do not join nucleotides sequentially. Hence option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: न्यूक्लिक अम्लों में एक न्यूक्लियोटाइड की 3'-OH और दूसरे की 5'-OH के बीच फॉस्फेट समूह एस्टर बंध बनाकर फॉस्फोडाइएस्टर बंध निर्मित करता है। अतः सही उत्तर D है।

questions.text: स्कर्वी रोग किसकी कमी के कारण होता है?
questions.text_english: Scurvy is caused due to deficiency of
questions.solution: Scurvy is a disease caused by deficiency of Vitamin C, which is chemically known as ascorbic acid. It is characterized by bleeding gums, weakness, and poor wound healing because Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis. Vitamin B1 deficiency causes Beriberi; Vitamin B2 deficiency causes Ariboflavinosis; Glutamic acid is an amino acid, not a vitamin. Hence option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: स्कर्वी रोग विटामिन C (ऐस्कॉर्बिक अम्ल) की कमी से होता है। इसमें मसूड़ों से खून आना और घाव देर से भरना जैसे लक्षण प्रकट होते हैं। अतः सही उत्तर C है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया में यदि अभिकारक की सांद्रता दोगुनी हो जाती है, तो इसका अर्धायुकाल भी दोगुना हो जाता है।
कारण (R) : प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया में अर्धायुकाल अभिकारक की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता पर निर्भर नहीं करता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In a first order reaction, if the concentration of the reactant is doubled, its half-life is also doubled.
Reason (R): The half-life of a reaction does not depend upon the initial concentration of the reactant in a first order reaction.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: For a first order reaction, t1/2 = 0.693/k. This formula shows that the half-life depends only on the rate constant k and is completely independent of the initial concentration. Therefore, even if the concentration is doubled, the half-life remains unchanged — it does NOT double. So Assertion (A) is false. However, Reason (R) correctly states that half-life of a first order reaction is independent of the initial concentration, which is a true statement. Hence option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए t1/2 = 0.693/k, जो प्रारंभिक सांद्रता पर निर्भर नहीं करता। अतः अभिकथन (A) गलत है लेकिन कारण (R) सही है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : Cu तनु खनिज अम्ल के साथ अभिक्रिया करके H2 मुक्त नहीं कर सकता।
कारण (R) : Cu का इलेक्ट्रोड विभव धनात्मक है।

Assertion (A): Cu cannot liberate H2 on reaction with dilute mineral acids.
Reason (R): Cu has positive electrode potential.

options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

questions.solution: Copper (Cu) has a standard electrode potential of +0.34 V, which is positive, meaning Cu is less reactive than hydrogen and lies below hydrogen in the electrochemical series. A metal can displace H2 from dilute acids only if its electrode potential is negative (i.e., it is above hydrogen in the activity series). Since Cu has a positive electrode potential, it cannot reduce H⁺ ions to H2. Therefore both the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly and completely explains why the Assertion (A) is true. Hence option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: Cu का मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव +0.34 V है (धनात्मक), अतः यह हाइड्रोजन से कम क्रियाशील है और तनु अम्ल से H2 मुक्त नहीं कर सकता। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।

Assertion (A): Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis.
Reason (R): Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reaction with the anion formed by phthalimide.

questions.solution: Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis works by the nucleophilic substitution of an alkyl halide with the potassium phthalimide anion. Aryl halides (C6H5X) are extremely resistant to nucleophilic substitution reactions because the C–X bond in aryl halides has partial double bond character due to resonance with the benzene ring, making the carbon less electrophilic, and the rigid planar ring system prevents backside attack (SN2). Therefore, aromatic primary amines cannot be made this way. Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R correctly explains A. Option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: गैब्रिएल संश्लेषण में ऐरिल हैलाइड, थैलिमाइड ऋणायन के साथ नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन नहीं करते क्योंकि C-X बंध में आंशिक द्विबंध लक्षण होता है। अतः दोनों अभिकथन और कारण सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : विटामिन D हमारे शरीर में संचित नहीं हो सकता है।
कारण (R) : विटामिन D वसा में घुलनशील विटामिन है और मूत्र के माध्यम से शरीर से बाहर नहीं निकलता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Vitamin D cannot be stored in our body.
Reason (R): Vitamin D is fat soluble vitamin and is not excreted from the body in urine.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin (A, D, E, K are fat-soluble). Because it is fat-soluble, it can be stored in adipose (fat) tissue and the liver for extended periods. Therefore, Assertion (A) — that Vitamin D cannot be stored — is FALSE. Vitamin D can actually be stored in the body, unlike water-soluble vitamins which are rapidly excreted. Reason (R) is TRUE: Vitamin D is indeed fat-soluble and is not excreted in urine. Hence option D (Assertion false, Reason true) is the correct answer.

questions.text_english:
(A) The rate constant for a zero order reaction A → P is 0.0030 mol L⁻¹s⁻¹. How long will it take for the initial concentration of A to fall from 0.10 M to 0.075 M?

OR

(B) The decomposition of NH3 on platinum surface is zero order reaction. What are the rates of production of N2 and H2 if k = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹?

key_points: Part A: For zero order reaction, t = ([A]0 - [A]t) / k = (0.10 - 0.075) / 0.0030 = 8.33 s
Part B: Reaction is 2NH3 → N2 + 3H2; Rate of reaction = k = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹; Rate of production of N2 = k/2 = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹; Rate of H2 = 3k/2 = 7.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹

questions.solution:
Part (A): For a zero order reaction, the integrated rate equation is: [A]t = [A]0 - kt. Rearranging, t = ([A]0 - [A]t) / k. Substituting the values: t = (0.10 - 0.075) / 0.0030 = 0.025 / 0.0030 = 8.33 seconds.

Part (B): The balanced equation for decomposition of NH3 is: 2NH3 → N2 + 3H2. For zero order, the rate of reaction = k = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹. The rate of production of N2 = k/2 = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹. The rate of production of H2 = (3/2) × k = 3 × 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ / 2 = 3.75 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹.

questions.text_english: Define the following terms:

key_points: A reaction that is not truly first order but behaves as first order because the concentration of one or more reactants remains effectively constant throughout the reaction.

sub_questions.solution: A pseudo first order reaction is a reaction which is actually of higher order (usually second order) but appears to follow first order kinetics because the concentration of one reactant is present in such large excess that it remains essentially constant throughout the reaction. For example, the hydrolysis of ethyl acetate: CH3COOC2H5 + H2O → CH3COOH + C2H5OH. Here, water is in large excess, so its concentration remains constant, and the reaction behaves as first order with respect to the ester only.

key_points: The half-life of a reaction is the time required for the concentration of a reactant to fall to half its initial value.

sub_questions.solution: The half-life period of a reaction (t1/2) is defined as the time required for the concentration of a reactant to decrease to half of its initial concentration. For a first order reaction, t1/2 = 0.693/k (independent of initial concentration), and for a zero order reaction, t1/2 = [A]0 / 2k (depends on initial concentration).

sub_questions.text_english: Transition elements generally form coloured compounds.

key_points: Transition elements have partially filled d-orbitals. Ligands cause d-d splitting; d-d transitions absorb visible light and transmit complementary colour.

sub_questions.solution: Transition elements generally form coloured compounds because they have incompletely filled d-orbitals. When ligands surround the metal ion, they cause crystal field splitting of the d-orbitals into two energy levels. Electrons can absorb light in the visible region and undergo d-d transitions from a lower energy d-level to a higher energy d-level. The complementary colour of the absorbed light is transmitted, imparting colour to the compound.

sub_questions.text_english: Zinc is not regarded as a transition element.

key_points: Transition elements are defined as those having partially filled d-orbitals in their ground state or in their commonly occurring oxidation states. Zinc (Zn²⁺) has a completely filled d¹⁰ configuration and hence is not a transition element.

sub_questions.solution: Zinc is not regarded as a transition element because transition elements are defined as elements having incompletely filled d-orbitals either in the ground state (atom) or in any of their commonly occurring ions. Zinc (Z=30) has the ground state configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰4s², and its most common ion Zn²⁺ has the configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰ — a completely filled d-subshell. Since there are no partially filled d-orbitals, Zn does not exhibit typical transition metal properties and is not classified as a transition element.

sub_questions.text: हैलोजन यौगिकों के निम्नलिखित युगल में से कौन सा यौगिक तीव्रता से SN1 अभिक्रिया करेगा और क्यों? (tert-butyl chloride तथा isobutyl chloride का युगल)
sub_questions.text_english: In the following pair of halogen compounds, which compound undergoes SN1 reaction faster and why? (tert-butyl chloride and isobutyl chloride as shown in the diagram)

key_points: tert-Butyl chloride (2-chloro-2-methylpropane) undergoes SN1 faster because it forms a stable tertiary carbocation intermediate.

sub_questions.solution: tert-Butyl chloride (2-chloro-2-methylpropane) undergoes SN1 reaction faster. The SN1 mechanism proceeds through the formation of a carbocation intermediate. tert-Butyl chloride ionizes to form a tertiary carbocation, which is highly stabilized by three alkyl groups through hyperconjugation and inductive effect. Isobutyl chloride forms only a primary carbocation upon ionization, which is far less stable. Since the rate of SN1 depends on the stability of the carbocation formed, the tertiary compound reacts faster.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को SN2 प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति उनकी अभिक्रियाशीलता के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए: 2-ब्रोमो-2-मेथिलब्यूटेन, 1-ब्रोमोपेन्टेन, 2-ब्रोमोपेन्टेन
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their reactivity towards SN2 displacement: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane, 1-Bromopentane, 2-Bromopentane.

key_points: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane < 2-Bromopentane < 1-Bromopentane

sub_questions.solution: SN2 reactions proceed through backside attack of the nucleophile, so steric hindrance at the reaction centre is the key factor. 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is a tertiary halide — the central carbon is surrounded by three alkyl groups, creating maximum steric hindrance — it is the least reactive. 2-Bromopentane is a secondary halide with moderate steric hindrance. 1-Bromopentane is a primary halide with the least steric hindrance, making it most reactive towards SN2. Therefore the increasing order of reactivity is: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane < 2-Bromopentane < 1-Bromopentane.

questions.text: 25°C पर पानी का संतृप्त वाष्प दाब 24 mm Hg है। उसी ताप पर यूरिया के 5% जलीय विलयन का संतृप्त वाष्य दाब ज्ञात कीजिए। (यूरिया का मोलर द्रव्यमान = 60 g mol⁻¹)
questions.text_english: At 25°C the saturated vapour pressure of water is 24 mm Hg. Find the saturated vapour pressure of a 5% aqueous solution of urea at the same temperature. (Molar mass of urea = 60 g mol⁻¹)

key_points: 5% aqueous solution means 5 g urea in 100 g solution, so 95 g water
Moles of urea = 5/60 = 0.0833 mol
Moles of water = 95/18 = 5.278 mol
By Raoult's law: (P° - Ps)/P° = x_solute; Ps = P°(1 - x_solute) = 24(1 - 0.01554) = 23.63 mm Hg

questions.solution: A 5% aqueous solution of urea means 5 g of urea is dissolved in 95 g of water (total 100 g solution). Moles of urea = 5/60 = 0.0833 mol. Moles of water = 95/18 = 5.278 mol. Mole fraction of urea (x2) = 0.0833/(0.0833 + 5.278) = 0.0833/5.361 = 0.01554. Applying Raoult's law: (P° - Ps)/P° = x2, so Ps = P°(1 - x2) = 24 × (1 - 0.01554) = 24 × 0.9845 = 23.63 mm Hg. Therefore, the saturated vapour pressure of the urea solution at 25°C is approximately 23.63 mm Hg.

Conductivity (κ) = 1/ρ = 0.01 S m⁻¹

Since the 3d orbitals are completely filled (3d¹⁰) and there are no unpaired electrons, the complex is diamagnetic.

key_points: Enantiomers: stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other
Racemic mixture: an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers that has no net optical rotation

sub_questions.solution: Enantiomers are pairs of stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other, like left and right hands. They have identical physical properties (melting point, boiling point, solubility) but differ in the direction in which they rotate plane-polarized light — one rotates it clockwise (+) and the other anticlockwise (-). A racemic mixture (or racemate) is an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers of a chiral compound. Since the optical rotations of the two enantiomers cancel each other out, a racemic mixture shows zero net optical rotation and is optically inactive.

sub_questions.text: क्लोरोबेंज़ीन नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के प्रति प्रतिरोधी क्यों है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is chlorobenzene resistant to nucleophilic substitution reaction?

key_points: C–Cl bond has partial double bond character due to resonance; carbon of C–Cl bond is not sufficiently electrophilic; rigid planar ring prevents backside attack

sub_questions.solution: Chlorobenzene is resistant to nucleophilic substitution because the lone pair of electrons on the chlorine atom donates into the benzene ring through resonance, giving the C–Cl bond a partial double bond character. This makes the bond shorter and stronger than a normal C–Cl single bond. Additionally, the carbon bearing the Cl is not sufficiently electrophilic for nucleophilic attack (since electron density is delocalized into it from Cl via resonance), and the rigid planar ring structure of benzene prevents backside attack required for SN2. Therefore, chlorobenzene does not undergo nucleophilic substitution under normal conditions.

key_points: Carbonyl compound + H2N-NH2 → hydrazone; hydrazone + KOH/ethylene glycol/heat → alkane + N2

A brown chromium complex is first formed, which on hydrolysis with water gives benzaldehyde. Equation: C6H5CH3 + 2CrO2Cl2 → C6H5CH(CrOCl2OH)2 → (H2O) → C6H5CHO + CrO(OH)Cl.

When treated with concentrated NaOH, one molecule of the aldehyde is oxidized to the corresponding carboxylic acid (as its sodium salt) while another molecule is simultaneously reduced to the corresponding primary alcohol. This is a disproportionation reaction. Equation: 2HCHO + NaOH → HCOONa + CH3OH (formaldehyde gives sodium formate and methanol).

questions.text: निम्नलिखित पदों को परिभाषित कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Define the following terms:

key_points: The covalent bond formed between the anomeric carbon (C-1) of one monosaccharide and the hydroxyl group of another monosaccharide with the loss of a water molecule is called glycosidic linkage.

sub_questions.solution: A glycosidic linkage is the covalent bond formed between two monosaccharide units when the -OH group on the anomeric carbon (C-1) of one monosaccharide reacts with the -OH group of another monosaccharide with the elimination of a water molecule. For example, in sucrose, glucose and fructose are joined by an alpha-1,2-glycosidic linkage. This type of bond forms the backbone of disaccharides and polysaccharides.

key_points: The equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose obtained by hydrolysis of sucrose is called invert sugar.

sub_questions.solution: Invert sugar is the equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose produced by the hydrolysis of sucrose (cane sugar). The term 'invert' is used because sucrose is dextrorotatory (+66.5°), but upon hydrolysis the resulting mixture is laevorotatory (-19.8°) due to the strong laevorotation of fructose. This change in the sign of optical rotation from dextro to laevo during hydrolysis is called inversion, and the product is called invert sugar. Honey is a natural source of invert sugar.

key_points: Oligosaccharides are carbohydrates that yield 2 to 10 monosaccharide units on hydrolysis.

sub_questions.solution: Oligosaccharides are carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units upon hydrolysis. The monosaccharide units are joined together by glycosidic linkages. They are further classified based on the number of monosaccharide units: disaccharides (2 units, e.g., sucrose, maltose, lactose), trisaccharides (3 units), and so on up to decasaccharides (10 units). Sucrose and maltose are the most common examples of oligosaccharides.

questions.text: शुद्ध विलायक से विलयन में अथवा तनु विलयन से सांद्र विलयन में अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली के माध्यम से विलायक का स्वतः प्रवर्तित प्रवाह परासरण कहलाता है। परासरण परिघटना को एक ही आकार के दो अंडों को लेकर प्रदर्शित किया जा सकता है। अंडे में खोल के नीचे और अंडे के पदार्थ के चारों ओर की झिल्ली अर्धपारगम्य होती है। अंडे को तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल में डालकर बाहरी कठोर खोल को हटाया जा सकता है। कठोर खोल को हटाने के बाद एक अंडे को आसुत जल में और दूसरे को संतृप्त नमक के घोल में रखा जाता है। कुछ समय बाद, आसुत जल में रखा अंडा फूल जाता है, जबकि नमक के घोल में रखा अंडा सिकुड़ जाता है। परासरण को रोकने के लिए लगाया गया बाह्य दाब, परासरण दाब (एक अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म) कहलाता है। प्रतिलोम परासरण तब होता है जब लगाया गया बाह्य दाब परासरण दाब से अधिक हो जाता है।
questions.text_english: The spontaneous flow of the solvent through a semipermeable membrane from a pure solvent to a solution or from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution is called osmosis. The phenomenon of osmosis can be demonstrated by taking two eggs of the same size. In an egg, the membrane below the shell and around the egg material is semipermeable. The outer hard shell can be removed by putting the egg in dilute hydrochloric acid. After removing the hard shell, one egg is placed in distilled water and the other in a saturated salt solution. After some time, the egg placed in distilled water swells-up while the egg placed in salt solution shrinks. The external pressure applied to stop the osmosis is termed as osmotic pressure (a colligative property). Reverse osmosis takes place when the applied external pressure becomes larger than the osmotic pressure.

sub_questions.text: प्रतिलोम परासरण को परिभाषित कीजिए। एक अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली (SPM) का नाम बताइए जिसका उपयोग प्रतिलोम परासरण की प्रक्रिया में किया जा सकता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Define reverse osmosis. Name one SPM which can be used in the process of reverse osmosis.

key_points: Reverse osmosis: flow of solvent from solution to pure solvent when external pressure greater than osmotic pressure is applied
SPM example: cellulose acetate membrane

sub_questions.solution: Reverse osmosis is the process in which the solvent flows from a solution (more concentrated) to the pure solvent (less concentrated) through a semipermeable membrane when an external pressure greater than the osmotic pressure is applied on the solution side. It is essentially the reversal of normal osmosis. This process is widely used for desalination of sea water to obtain pure drinking water. Cellulose acetate membrane is one example of a semipermeable membrane used in reverse osmosis.

sub_questions.text: जब लाल रुधिर कोशिकाओं (RBC) को 0.5% NaCl विलयन में रखा जाता है तो आप क्या होने की अपेक्षा करते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: What do you expect to happen when red blood corpuscles (RBC's) are placed in 0.5% NaCl solution?

key_points: 0.5% NaCl is hypotonic relative to blood; water enters RBCs by osmosis; cells swell and may lyse (haemolysis)

sub_questions.solution: Normal blood has an effective NaCl concentration of about 0.9%. A 0.5% NaCl solution is hypotonic (less concentrated) compared to the cell fluid inside RBCs. When RBCs are placed in this solution, water flows into the cells through osmosis (from the hypotonic solution into the hypertonic cell interior). The RBCs swell up. If the external concentration is sufficiently low, the cells may burst — a process called haemolysis.

sub_questions.text: 1 M KCl अथवा 1 M यूरिया विलयन में से किसका परासरण दाब अधिक होगा। अपने उत्तर का औचित्य दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following will have higher osmotic pressure in 1 M KCl or 1 M urea solution. Justify your answer.

key_points: 1 M KCl has higher osmotic pressure because it is an electrolyte that dissociates into K⁺ and Cl⁻, giving effectively 2 M particles; urea is non-electrolyte with 1 M particles

sub_questions.solution: 1 M KCl will have higher osmotic pressure than 1 M urea. Osmotic pressure is a colligative property that depends on the number of solute particles in solution. KCl is a strong electrolyte that completely dissociates: KCl → K⁺ + Cl⁻, giving effectively 2 moles of particles per mole dissolved (van't Hoff factor i = 2). Urea is a non-electrolyte and does not dissociate (i = 1). Therefore, 1 M KCl produces twice as many particles as 1 M urea, resulting in a much higher osmotic pressure.

sub_questions.text: परासरण दाब एक अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म क्यों है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why osmotic pressure is a colligative property?

key_points: Osmotic pressure depends on the number of solute particles (moles) in solution, not on their nature or identity.

sub_questions.solution: Osmotic pressure is a colligative property because it depends only on the number of solute particles (moles or concentration) dissolved in a given volume of solution, and not on the nature, size, or chemical identity of the solute particles. The relationship π = iMRT shows that osmotic pressure (π) depends on the molar concentration (M) and van't Hoff factor (i, which accounts for the number of particles), confirming that it is a counting property of solute particles.

questions.text: ऐमीनों में नाइट्रोजन परमाणु पर एकाकी इलेक्ट्रॉन युग्म होता है जिसके कारण वे लुईस क्षारक की तरह व्यवहार करते हैं। Kb का मान जितना अधिक होगा या pKb का मान जितना कम होगा, क्षारक उतना ही प्रबल होगा। ऐल्कोहॉल, ईथर, एस्टर आदि की तुलना में ऐमीन अधिक क्षारकीय हैं। ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन का क्षारकीय गुण ऐल्किल प्रतिस्थापन की वृद्धि के साथ-साथ बढ़ना चाहिए। लेकिन यह नियमित रूप से नहीं होता है क्योंकि द्वितीयक ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन अप्रत्याशित रूप से जलीय विलयन में तृतीयक ऐमीन की तुलना में अधिक क्षारकीय होता है। ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया और ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन की तुलना में दुर्बल क्षारक होते हैं। इलेक्ट्रॉन मुक्त करने वाले समूह जैसे - CH3, -OCH3, -NH2 आदि क्षारकीयता को बढ़ाते हैं जबकि इलेक्ट्रॉन खींचने (अपनयन) वाले प्रतिस्थापित समूह जैसे - NO2, -CN, हैलोजन आदि, ऐमीन की क्षारकीयता को कम करते हैं। इन प्रतिस्थापनों का प्रभाव m⁻ स्थितियों की तुलना में p⁻ पर अधिक होता है।
questions.text_english: Amines have a lone pair of electrons on nitrogen atom due to which they behave as Lewis base. Greater the value of Kb or smaller the value of pKb, stronger is the base. Amines are more basic than alcohols, ethers, esters, etc. The basic character of aliphatic amines should increase with the increase of alkyl substitution. But it does not occur in a regular manner as a secondary aliphatic amine is unexpectedly more basic than a tertiary amine in aqueous solutions. Aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia and aliphatic amines. Electron releasing groups such as -CH3, -OCH3, -NH2, etc., increase the basicity while electron-withdrawing substituents such as -NO2, -CN, halogens etc., decrease the basicity of amines. The effect of these substitute is more at p⁻ than at m⁻ position.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित को उनके क्षारकीय गुणों के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए। कारण दीजिए। (aniline, 4-nitroaniline, 4-methylaniline shown as structures)
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following in the increasing order of their basic character. Give reason: (aniline, 4-nitroaniline, 4-methylaniline shown as structures)

key_points: 4-nitroaniline < aniline < 4-methylaniline
-NO2 at para withdraws electrons decreasing basicity; -CH3 at para donates electrons increasing basicity

sub_questions.solution: The increasing order of basic character is: 4-nitroaniline < aniline < 4-methylaniline. The -NO2 group at the para position is a strong electron-withdrawing group. It withdraws electron density from the nitrogen atom of the amine through resonance and inductive effects, making the lone pair on N less available for donation to an acid — hence 4-nitroaniline is the weakest base. The -CH3 group at the para position in 4-methylaniline is an electron-donating group (by hyperconjugation and inductive effect), which increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom, making it a stronger base than aniline. Hence the order is: 4-nitroaniline < aniline < 4-methylaniline.

sub_questions.text: मेथिलऐमीन की तुलना में ऐनिलीन का pKb मान अधिक क्यों होता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why pKb of aniline is more than that of methylamine?

key_points: In aniline, lone pair of N is delocalized into benzene ring via resonance; less available for protonation; hence weaker base, higher pKb

sub_questions.solution: The pKb of aniline (9.40) is much higher than that of methylamine (3.36), meaning aniline is a much weaker base. In aniline, the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is delocalized into the benzene ring through resonance. This delocalization makes the lone pair less available for accepting a proton (less basic). In methylamine, the -CH3 group donates electrons to nitrogen by inductive effect, making the lone pair more available and methylamine a stronger base. Therefore, aniline has a higher pKb than methylamine.

sub_questions.text: जलीय विलयन में निम्नलिखित को उनके क्षारकीय गुणों के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए। कारण दीजिए: (CH3)3N, (CH3)2NH, NH3, CH3NH2
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following in the increasing order of their basic character in an aqueous solution: (CH3)3N, (CH3)2NH, NH3, CH3NH2

key_points: NH3 < (CH3)3N < CH3NH2 < (CH3)2NH

sub_questions.solution: In aqueous solution, the order of basic strength is: NH3 < (CH3)3N < CH3NH2 < (CH3)2NH. In aqueous solution, solvation (hydration) of the conjugate acid plays an important role. Although (CH3)3N has the highest electron density on N due to three methyl groups, its conjugate acid [(CH3)3NH⁺] is poorly solvated (poorly hydrated) because the bulky methyl groups hinder hydrogen bonding with water. (CH3)2NH forms the most stable solvated conjugate acid due to a balance between electron donation by two methyl groups and effective solvation, making it the strongest base. CH3NH2 is stronger than NH3 due to the electron-donating methyl group. Hence the increasing order is: NH3 < (CH3)3N < CH3NH2 < (CH3)2NH.

questions.text_english:
(A) (a) Give IUPAC name of CH3 - CH = CH - CHO. (b) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between propanal and propanone. (c) How will you convert the following: (i) Toluene to benzoic acid (ii) Ethanol to propan-2-ol (iii) Propanal to 2-hydroxy propanoic acid

OR

(b) ? + (i)O3, (ii)Zn-H2O → 2 × cyclopentanone (c) Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid + SOCl2 (Δ) → ? (d) Cyclohexane bearing CHO and COOH groups + NaCN/HCl → ? (e) Benzene → acetophenone

key_points: Part A(a): But-2-enal
Part A(b): Tollens test or Fehling test — propanal gives silver mirror / brick red precipitate; propanone gives no reaction
Part A(c)(i): Toluene + KMnO4/H⁺ or acidic K2Cr2O7 → Benzoic acid

Part A(c)(ii): Ethanol → (PBr3) → bromoethane → (Mg/dry ether) → ethyl Grignard → (CH2O then H3O+) → propan-1-ol? Actually ethanol to propan-2-ol: CH3CH2OH → (oxidize) → CH3CHO → (HCN) → CH3CH(OH)CN → (H3O+) → CH3CH(OH)COOH? No: ethanol to propan-2-ol via: CH3CHO + CH3MgBr → propan-2-ol

questions.image_description: Part B shows 5 reaction schemes with structural formulae: (a) cyclobutanone reacting with hydroxylamine; (b) an unknown compound undergoing ozonolysis to give two cyclopentanone molecules; (c) cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid with SOCl2; (d) cyclohexane with CHO and COOH groups reacting with NaCN/HCl; (e) benzene converting to acetophenone (phenyl methyl ketone).
questions.solution:
Part A(a): The IUPAC name of CH3-CH=CH-CHO is but-2-enal. The parent chain has 4 carbons with an aldehyde at C-1 and a double bond between C-2 and C-3.

Part A(b): To distinguish propanal from propanone, use Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) or Fehling's solution. Propanal is an aldehyde and gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent (or brick-red precipitate with Fehling's solution). Propanone is a ketone and gives no reaction with either reagent.

Part A(c)(i): Toluene to Benzoic acid: Toluene is oxidized with acidic KMnO4 or acidic K2Cr2O7 (or conc. HNO3+H2SO4 followed by oxidation). The methyl group is oxidized to -COOH: C6H5CH3 → (KMnO4/H⁺, heat) → C6H5COOH.

Part A(c)(ii): Ethanol to Propan-2-ol: Ethanol is first oxidized to acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) using mild oxidant. Acetaldehyde reacts with CH3MgBr (methylmagnesium bromide, a Grignard reagent) to give propan-2-ol after acid hydrolysis: CH3CHO + CH3MgBr → CH3CH(OMgBr)CH3 → (H3O+) → CH3CH(OH)CH3.

Part A(c)(iii): Propanal to 2-Hydroxy propanoic acid (Lactic acid): Propanal (CH3CH2CHO) reacts with HCN to form cyanohydrin: CH3CH2CHO + HCN → CH3CH2CH(OH)CN. The cyanohydrin on hydrolysis with dilute acid gives 2-hydroxypropanoic acid (lactic acid): CH3CH2CH(OH)CN + H2O/H⁺ → CH3CH2CH(OH)COOH.

Part B: (a) Cyclobutanone + HO-NH2 + H⁺ → Cyclobutanone oxime (cyclobutanone oxime with =N-OH). (b) The missing starting material for ozonolysis that gives 2 molecules of cyclopentanone is cyclopentene joined by a double bond — actually it is cyclodecene (or a compound with a ring double bond): the compound is 1,2-di(cyclopentyl)alkene? The compound undergoing ozonolysis to give 2 cyclopentanone molecules is cyclopentyl methylenecyclopentane or more correctly it is cyclopentadiene dimer opening — the correct starting material is 1,2-dicyclopentylidene? Actually the simplest answer: the ozonolysis of a cyclic alkene with one double bond gives one dicarbonyl compound; but two molecules of cyclopentanone means two separate rings formed, so the starting material is a bicyclic or spiro compound. The most likely answer is 1,1'-bi(cyclopentyl)ethylene, i.e., the starting material is 1-(cyclopentylidene)cyclopentane. (c) Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid + SOCl2 (heat) → cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic anhydride (the cyclic anhydride). (d) The cyclohexane with both CHO and COOH reacts with NaCN/HCl — NaCN adds to the CHO (cyanohydrin formation) while COOH remains; product is the cyanohydrin: cyclohexane with CH(OH)CN and COOH groups. (e) Benzene → Acetophenone: Friedel-Crafts acylation: C6H6 + CH3COCl → (AlCl3 catalyst) → C6H5COCH3 (acetophenone) + HCl.

questions.text:
(A) (a) 25°C पर निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया के लिए मानक गिब्ज़ ऊर्जा (ΔrG°) का परिकलन कीजिए: Au(s) + Ca²⁺(1M) → Au³⁺(1M) + Ca(s); E°Au³⁺/Au = +1.5 V, E°Ca²⁺/Ca = −2.87 V। प्रागुक्ति कीजिए कि 25°C पर अभिक्रिया स्वतः प्रवर्तित होगी या नहीं। [1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹] (b) मलिन चाँदी में Ag2S होता है। क्या इस मलिनता को मलिन चाँदी के बर्तन को एल्युमिनियम पैन में रखकर हटाया जा सकता है, जिसमें NaCl जैसा निष्क्रिय विद्युत अपघटनी विलयन भरा हो? अर्ध अभिक्रिया के लिए मानक इलेक्ट्रॉड विभव: Ag2S(s) + 2e⁻ → 2Ag(s) + S²⁻ के लिए −0.71 V है और Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → 2Al(s) के लिए −1.66 V है।

अथवा

(B) (a) निम्नलिखित को परिभाषित कीजिए: (i) सेल विभव (ii) ईंधन सेल (b) निम्नलिखित सेल के emf की 25°C पर गणना करें: Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(0.1M)||Cd²⁺(0.01M)|Cd(s); E°Cd²⁺/Cd = −0.40 V, E°Zn²⁺/Zn = −0.76 V [log 10 = 1]
questions.text_english:
(A) (a) Calculate the standard Gibbs energy (ΔrG°) of the following reaction at 25°C: Au(s) + Ca²⁺(1M) → Au³⁺(1M) + Ca(s); E°Au³⁺/Au = +1.5 V, E°Ca²⁺/Ca = −2.87 V. Predict whether the reaction will be spontaneous or not at 25°C. [1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹] (b) Tarnished silver contains Ag2S. Can this tarnish be removed by placing tarnished silverware in an aluminium pan containing an inert electrolytic solution such as NaCl? The standard electrode potential for half reaction: Ag2S(s) + 2e⁻ → 2Ag(s) + S²⁻ is −0.71 V and for Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → 2Al(s) is −1.66 V.

OR

(B) (a) Define the following: (i) Cell potential (ii) Fuel cell (b) Calculate emf of the following cell at 25°C: Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(0.1M)||Cd²⁺(0.01M)|Cd(s); E°Cd²⁺/Cd = −0.40 V, E°Zn²⁺/Zn = −0.76 V [log 10 = 1]

key_points: Part A(a): E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = E°Ca²⁺/Ca - E°Au³⁺/Au = -2.87 - 1.5 = -4.37 V; n=6; ΔrG° = -nFE°cell = -6 × 96500 × (-4.37) = +2530470 J/mol = +2530.47 kJ/mol; positive ΔrG° means non-spontaneous
Part A(b): E°cell for Al reducing Ag2S: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = -0.71 - (-1.66) = +0.95 V; positive E°cell means reaction is spontaneous; tarnish can be removed
Part B(a)(i): Cell potential is the potential difference between the two electrodes of an electrochemical cell
Part B(a)(ii): Fuel cell is an electrochemical cell that converts chemical energy of combustion of fuels directly into electrical energy

questions.solution:
Part A(a): The given reaction is: Au(s) + Ca²⁺(1M) → Au³⁺(1M) + Ca(s). Here Ca is oxidized (anode) and Au³⁺ is reduced (cathode) — but wait, as written Au is oxidized and Ca²⁺ is reduced. Cathode (reduction): Ca²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Ca, E° = -2.87 V. Anode (oxidation): Au → Au³⁺ + 3e⁻, E°oxidation = -1.5 V. To balance electrons: multiply cathode by 3 and anode by 2. E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = (-2.87) - (+1.5) = -4.37 V. n = 6 (LCM of 2 and 3). ΔrG° = -nFE°cell = -6 × 96500 × (-4.37) = +2,530,470 J mol⁻¹ ≈ +2530.47 kJ mol⁻¹. Since ΔrG° is positive, the reaction is non-spontaneous.

Part A(b): The cell reaction would be: Al reduces Ag2S. Cathode: Ag2S + 2e⁻ → 2Ag + S²⁻, E° = -0.71 V. Anode: Al → Al³⁺ + 3e⁻, E°oxidation = +1.66 V. E°cell = -0.71 - (-1.66) = +0.95 V. Since E°cell is positive, the reaction is spontaneous. Therefore yes, the tarnish (Ag2S) can be removed by placing the silverware in an aluminium pan with NaCl solution — Al acts as a reducing agent and reduces Ag2S back to metallic Ag.

Part B(a)(i): Cell potential (EMF of a cell) is defined as the potential difference between the two electrodes (cathode and anode) of an electrochemical cell. It is measured in volts and equals E°cathode - E°anode for standard conditions.

Part B(a)(ii): A fuel cell is an electrochemical cell (galvanic cell) that converts the chemical energy released during the combustion of fuels like hydrogen, methane, or methanol directly into electrical energy. For example, in a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell: H2 + ½O2 → H2O, producing electricity continuously as long as fuel is supplied.

Part B(b): Cell: Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(0.1M)||Cd²⁺(0.01M)|Cd(s). E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = E°Cd²⁺/Cd - E°Zn²⁺/Zn = (-0.40) - (-0.76) = +0.36 V. Using Nernst equation: E_cell = E°cell - (0.0591/n) log Q. Here n = 2, Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Cd²⁺] = 0.1/0.01 = 10. E_cell = 0.36 - (0.0591/2) × log 10 = 0.36 - (0.02955 × 1) = 0.36 - 0.02955 = 0.3305 V ≈ 0.33 V.

(A) An organic compound 'A', molecular formula C2H6O oxidises with CrO3 to form a compound 'B'. Compound 'B' on warming with iodine and aqueous solution of NaOH gives a yellow precipitate of compound 'C'. When compound 'A' is heated with conc. H2SO4 at 413 K gives a compound 'D', which on reaction with excess HI gives compound 'E'. Identify compounds 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D' and 'E' and write chemical equations involved.

OR

(B) (a) Write chemical equations of the following reactions: (i) Phenol is treated with conc. HNO3 (ii) Propene is treated with B2H6 followed by oxidation by H2O2/OH⁻ (iii) Sodium t-butoxide is treated with CH3Cl (b) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol. (c) Arrange the following in increasing order of acid strength: phenol, ethanol, water

key_points: Part A: A = ethanol (CH3CH2OH); B = acetaldehyde (CH3CHO); C = iodoform (CHI3); D = diethyl ether (CH3CH2OCH2CH3); E = ethane (or iodoethane then ethane with excess HI)
Part B(b): Lucas test — butan-1-ol (primary) does not react immediately; butan-2-ol (secondary) turns turbid within 5 minutes
Part B(c): ethanol < water < phenol

questions.solution:
Part A: Compound A has molecular formula C2H6O and is oxidized by CrO3. The two possible structures are ethanol (CH3CH2OH) and dimethyl ether (CH3OCH3). Since CrO3 oxidizes alcohols (not ethers), A is ethanol. A (CH3CH2OH) → (CrO3) → B (CH3CHO, acetaldehyde). B (CH3CHO) on warming with I2 and NaOH (iodoform test) gives yellow precipitate C = CHI3 (iodoform). Equation: CH3CHO + 3I2 + 3NaOH → CHI3 + HCOONa + 3NaI + 2H2O. A (CH3CH2OH) heated with conc. H2SO4 at 413 K gives intermolecular dehydration to form D = CH3CH2OCH2CH3 (diethyl ether). Equation: 2CH3CH2OH → (conc. H2SO4, 413 K) → CH3CH2OCH2CH3 + H2O. D (diethyl ether) + excess HI → E. Ether cleavage with excess HI: CH3CH2OCH2CH3 + 2HI → 2CH3CH2I (iodoethane). With excess HI the iodoethane further reduces to ethane if conditions are drastic, but typically E = CH3CH2I (iodoethane). So: A = Ethanol; B = Acetaldehyde; C = Iodoform (CHI3); D = Diethyl ether; E = Iodoethane (CH3CH2I).

Part B(a)(i): Phenol + conc. HNO3 → 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid). Equation: C6H5OH + 3HNO3 → (conc. H2SO4) → C6H2(NO2)3OH + 3H2O.

Part B(a)(ii): Hydroboration-oxidation of propene: CH3CH=CH2 + B2H6 → (CH3CH2CH2)3B → (H2O2/OH⁻) → 3CH3CH2CH2OH (propan-1-ol). This gives anti-Markovnikov addition of water (propan-1-ol).

Part B(a)(iii): Sodium t-butoxide + CH3Cl: (CH3)3CONa + CH3Cl → (CH3)3COCH3 + NaCl. This gives methyl tert-butyl ether (Williamson synthesis).

Part B(b): Lucas test distinguishes butan-1-ol from butan-2-ol. Both are treated with Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2) at room temperature. Butan-2-ol (secondary alcohol) reacts within 5 minutes, turning the solution turbid due to formation of insoluble 2-chlorobutane. Butan-1-ol (primary alcohol) does not react at room temperature and the solution remains clear.

Part B(c): Increasing order of acid strength: ethanol < water < phenol. Ethanol is the weakest acid (pKa ≈ 16) because the ethyl group donates electrons, making it harder to release H⁺. Water (pKa ≈ 15.7) is slightly more acidic than ethanol. Phenol is the most acidic (pKa ≈ 10) because the phenoxide ion formed after losing H⁺ is stabilized by resonance with the benzene ring, making phenol a stronger acid than both water and ethanol.
